title: Graph-Attention Network for Cross-Domain Facial Expression Recognition
text:
Integrated ResNet-50 and Graph Attention Networks with adversarial domain alignment (MMD, CORAL, GRL). Achieved 74% mean accuracy across six datasets: RAF-DB, FER2013, CK+, JAFFE, ExpW, and SFEW2.0.
This work was presented at ACML 2025.
View code on GitHub

title: LDA-Based Grievance Mechanism Analysis
text:
Applied advanced LDA topic modelling to 2,957 grievance documents from UK Modern Slavery Act statements, identifying 18 optimal topics to analyse patterns in corporate disclosure practices.
View code on GitHub

title: Corporate Ethics Automation System
text:
Kaggle Agents Intensive hackathon entry: built a Google ADK automation tool to replicate KnowTheChain benchmark workflows in under 60 seconds using PDF extraction, sentiment analysis, correlation analysis, and regression.

title: RepoForge AI: Agentic Test Generation for Public Python Repositories
text:
Built a multi-agent system (an OrchestratorAgent plus specialised agents for ingestion, code analysis, API discovery, retrieval, test planning, and test writing) that scans public Git repositories and generates validated pytest suites.
Combined RAG over ChromaDB-indexed code chunks with Gemini-based generation, plus safety checks (secret redaction, unsafe-pattern blocking) to produce reviewable, downloadable test artifacts.

About


Research Associate | Deep Learning & Human-Centered AI


I am a Research Associate at the University of Sheffield, working on multi-agent AI systems for automated corporate ethics benchmarking and forced-labour risk assessment across global supply chains. My research combines deep learning, multimodal learning, and human-centered AI, with a particular focus on cross-domain facial expression recognition, affective computing, and socially responsible AI applications.


I hold an MSc in Computer Science (Distinction) from Manchester Metropolitan University, where my dissertation on deep learning-based cross-domain facial expression recognition scored 80/100. My work has been published in venues including Knowledge-Based Systems, ACML 2025, and IEEE Access, and I collaborate across disciplines at the intersection of AI, operations management, and social impact.


Before moving into research, I spent several years as a software engineer building enterprise applications, which now shapes how I approach building reliable, well-engineered AI systems rather than one-off research prototypes.
